outputs.explanation: Scatter plot in which each of the 141 points represents an individual sample; scatter plots are exempt from requiring additional overlaid individual points.
Scatter plot (each marker = one cell line/reporter mean ± s.d.); scatter plots are exempt from the individual-points requirement even when error bars denote variability.
Continuous density/line curves (normal distributions of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes); line plots are exempt since overlaying individual points would make them unreadable.
Box plots of ridge lengths, which are exempt by definition, but individual sample data points are additionally overlaid as dots on each box.
Polar histograms display distributions of phase differences (frequency/probability bars per cell line), not simple bar-chart averages, so individual point overlay is not required.
Polar histogram summarizing subtype-averaged phase differences as a distribution; histograms of this kind are not required to show individual data points.
Line/trace plot illustrating an example signal and its fitted decaying sinusoidal model; line plots of this kind are exempt from requiring individual point overlays.
Scatter plot where each marker represents one sample (n = 117) with error bars reflecting fit uncertainty; scatter plots are exempt from the individual-points requirement.
